newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on bearish export picture.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on bearish export picture.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower on bearish input from the export sector and on fund selling, traders said.
"There was a lot of talk of the lack of business," said Skip Searcy, wheat trading specialist for FIMAT Futures. "U.S. wheat is a specialized item right now, we can't get anything done right now."
USDA early Thursday said U.S. net export sales of wheat during the week ended January 9 totaled 177,500 tonnes, below expectations for 200,000 to 400,000 tonnes.
USDA said the net sales were above the previous week's level which was a low for the marketing year but remained 29 percent below the four-week average pace.
"Trinidad switched (71,000 tonnes) and that's significant," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
USDA confirmed that Trinidad switched 71,000 tonnes from the current 1996-97 marketing year to the 1997-98 shipment period.
Wheat closed 1/4 to three cents per bushel lower, with March down three at $3.87-1/4. May down 1-1/2 at $3.71-1/4.

Traders also cited bearish input from Algeria's purchase this week of 150,000 tonnes of wheat from France and none from the U.S. Also, Yemen this week bought 200,000 tonnes of flour from the EU and 200,000 tonnes of optional-origin white wheat.

Profit taking of the March/July spread was cited. The March gained substantially this week on harsh weather in the U.S. which slowed movement of wheat and boosted spot cash. On Thursday, the spread adjusted.
Refco Inc sold two million bushels of March and The Chicago Corp sold 1.2 million bushels of March, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 13,000 contracts, above the 11,552 traded Wednesday, according to the CBOT.

In wheat options, Prudential Securities sold 150 March $3.90 puts at 10 cents, ING Derivatives sold 150 March $3.90 puts at 10 cents and LFG Futures sold 150 July $3.50 calls at 21-1/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated by the CBOT at 5,000 contracts, slightly below the 5,676 traded Wednesday.
